approachQuestion.prompt:
Gather the Active Lamps

A binary array `lamps` records which positions on a straight rail are active. In one swap you may exchange any two positions, regardless of distance. Return the minimum swaps needed to make all ones occupy consecutive positions. Return zero if there are no ones.

Limits and assumptions:
• 0 ≤ n ≤ 200000; each lamps[i] is 0 or 1.
• The rail is not circular. Swaps are arbitrary, not restricted to adjacent positions. Return only the minimum count; leave the input unchanged.

Examples:
1. lamps = [1,0,1,0,1] → 1, by swapping positions 1 and 4.
2. lamps = [0,0] → 0.
3. lamps = [1,1,0] → 0.

Choose one approach.
constraints: The rail is not circular. Swaps are arbitrary, not restricted to adjacent positions. Return only the minimum count; leave the input unchanged.

options.text: Let t be the total number of ones. If t is zero return zero. Among all length-t intervals find the smallest number of zeros using a moving count. Return that count.
options.feedback: Any final block has length t. Each zero inside it can be exchanged with one outside, fixing one missing slot per swap.

options.text: Count t ones, build a prefix array of zero counts, and minimize the number of zeros in a length-t interval.
options.feedback: The transformation and answer are correct, but the prefix array is unnecessary for a single sequence of adjacent candidates.

options.text: Choose a target interval and sum the distances required to move each one into it using adjacent exchanges. Minimize that cost.
options.feedback: This solves a different operation. For [1,0,0,1], one arbitrary swap suffices, whereas adjacent movement needs two swaps.

options.text: Return the number of zeros between the first and last one.
options.feedback: For [1,0,0,1,1], the span contains two zeros, but one swap can create [0,0,1,1,1].

feedback.reason: A target block has t slots.
details: Count the total number t of ones. For t=0 return zero. Count zeros in the first t positions, then slide a length-t interval, subtracting the outgoing zero indicator and adding the incoming one. Return the least zero count.

A target block has t slots. Its z zeros correspond to exactly z ones outside, so z arbitrary swaps both suffice and are necessary. When t=0, the lamps are already gathered without creating a nonempty block.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only “Count holes in a target block” as specified in the method reveal. Choose the tightest worst-case running-time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Use unit-cost random access and arithmetic on machine words large enough for every index and sum.
Input is read-only and excluded from auxiliary space. The scalar or index-pair output is excluded; no candidate segment is copied.
The implementation is iterative with a constant call stack. No hashing is used; fixed alphabet arrays, when present, are direct indexed.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Two scans plus a rolling zero count use scalar state.
details: Every valid final block has exactly t slots. If it contains z zeros, exactly z ones are outside, so z arbitrary swaps are both necessary and sufficient. Two linear scans and a rolling zero count use O(n) time and scalar state.
“O(n²) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: A fixed-width zero count updates by one outgoing and one incoming indicator, avoiding a fresh scan for every t-slot block.
“O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: The method neither sorts lamp positions nor stores them; two scans use a scalar t and rolling zero count.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: The returned result is one swap count, and the method retains no position array or per-window history.
